objectives: Reason about WDM + amplifiers + telecom limits.

slides.title: Optical fiber: total internal reflection in glass
slides.body:
**Optical fiber**: thin (~125 µm) silica strand with core (higher index) + cladding (lower). Light propagates by TIR within core.

**Step-index profile**: core has uniform n_core; cladding uniform n_clad. Most common.
**Graded-index**: n decreases continuously from center; reduces modal dispersion.

**V-number (normalized frequency)**: V = (2π a / λ) × NA, where a = core radius, NA = √(n_core² − n_clad²).
- V < 2.405: single-mode (only LP_01 mode supported).
- V > 2.405: multi-mode (multiple LP_lm modes).

**Single-mode fiber (SMF)**:
- Core ~8-10 µm; NA ~0.12-0.14.
- ~1.5 dB/km loss at 1550 nm.
- Used for: long-haul telecom, fiber lasers, low-noise sensing.

**Multi-mode fiber (MMF)**:
- Core 50-62.5 µm; NA ~0.2.
- ~3 dB/km loss at 850 nm.
- Used for: short-distance (data center, building), high-power industrial.

**Attenuation windows**:
- 800-900 nm: ~3 dB/km; Si-photodetector compatible; data center.
- 1300 nm: ~0.4 dB/km; zero-dispersion in standard SMF.
- 1550 nm: ~0.2 dB/km; **lowest-loss window**; long-haul telecom; EDFA amplification.
- 1625-1675 nm: extended bands (S, C, L, U).

**Loss mechanisms**:
- Rayleigh scattering (~1/λ⁴): dominant in visible + near-IR.
- OH absorption (~1380 nm 'water peak'): mostly eliminated in modern fiber.
- Bend loss: macrobend (>10 mm radius) + microbend.
- Splice + connector loss: ~0.05-0.5 dB per joint.

Fiber is the lowest-loss communication medium known — ~0.2 dB/km vs ~1-10 dB/km coaxial or hundreds of dB/km wireless.

slides.title: Dispersion: pulse broadening in fiber
slides.body:
**Dispersion** causes pulse broadening — limits bandwidth-distance product.

**Modal dispersion** (multimode only): different modes have different group velocities → different arrival times. Step-index MMF: ~30 ns/km. Graded-index MMF: ~1 ns/km. Limits to short distances (~100 m at 10 Gbps).

**Chromatic dispersion**: different wavelengths propagate at different speeds in glass.
- **Material dispersion**: n(λ) of silica.
- **Waveguide dispersion**: mode-effective-index depends on fiber geometry.
- Total chromatic dispersion D measured in ps/(nm·km).
- **Zero-dispersion wavelength** for standard SMF: ~1310 nm. Telecom prefers 1550 nm (lowest loss) where D ≈ +17 ps/(nm·km).

**Dispersion management**:
- **Dispersion-shifted fiber (DSF)**: zero-D at 1550 nm. Tested but underperforms due to nonlinear effects.
- **Non-zero dispersion-shifted (NZDSF)**: small positive or negative D at 1550 to minimize nonlinear-cross-talk.
- **Dispersion-compensating fiber (DCF)**: high negative D to cancel positive D of standard SMF after long runs.
- **Fiber Bragg gratings**: chirped grating provides wavelength-dependent delay → dispersion compensation.
- **Electronic dispersion compensation**: at digital signal processing in coherent receivers; standard in 100G+ telecom.

**Polarization-mode dispersion (PMD)**: random birefringence; pulse split between polarizations. Typically 0.1-1 ps/√km. Limits 40G+ over long distance.

**Nonlinear effects** at high power:
- **Self-phase modulation (SPM)**: refractive index depends on intensity; pulse chirps itself.
- **Cross-phase modulation (XPM)**: between WDM channels.
- **Four-wave mixing (FWM)**: three frequencies combine to produce a fourth.
- **Brillouin + Raman scattering**: photon-phonon interactions; useful for amplification (Raman amps) but also loss + crosstalk.

slides.title: WDM + EDFA + coherent + 100G+
slides.body:
**Wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM)**: multiple wavelengths share one fiber.
- **DWDM (dense WDM)**: ITU-grid 50 or 100 GHz spacing; 80-96 channels in C-band (~1530-1565 nm).
- **CWDM (coarse)**: 20 nm spacing; cheaper components; metro networks.
- Total capacity: 100s of Tbps per fiber routinely.

**EDFA (Erbium-Doped Fiber Amplifier)**: Er-doped fiber section pumped at 980 or 1480 nm; provides ~25-30 dB gain across C-band. Enables fiber spans of 80-100+ km without optical-electrical-optical conversion. Revolutionized long-haul telecom (1990s onwards). Enabled transatlantic + transpacific cables at Tbps + ultimately Pbps capacity.

**Raman amplifiers**: distributed gain via stimulated Raman scattering using a co/counter-pumped fiber. Lower-noise alternative to EDFA; used in modern coherent + transoceanic links.

**Modulation formats**:
- **OOK (on-off keying)**: simplest; 10G era.
- **PAM4**: 4-level intensity; 100G data-center.
- **DP-QPSK** (dual-pol QPSK): coherent; 100G ULH telecom 2010s.
- **DP-16QAM**: 200G.
- **DP-64QAM**: 400-600G; Nyquist + complex DSP.
- **DP-256QAM**: 800-1.6T+; near-Shannon-limit.

**Coherent detection**: I + Q + polarization demodulated; digital signal processing for chromatic dispersion, PMD, polarization tracking, equalization, phase tracking. Used in modern 100G+. Replaced direct-detection for long-haul.

**Submarine cables**: ~10s Tbps per cable; 10-20 fiber pairs; 80-100 km repeater spacing with EDFA. ~500 cables connect global internet; ~95% of intercontinental traffic.

**Modern records**:
- Lab: ~150 Tbps over single fiber via massive WDM + DP-256QAM (NTT 2024).
- Commercial: ~12 Tbps per fiber + getting denser.
- Per-strand capacity has doubled every ~2.5 years historically.
- Limits: spectral bandwidth of EDFA (~10 THz), Shannon limit of nonlinear fiber, fiber-count + space-division multiplexing.

**Beyond standard fiber**:
- **Multi-core fiber (MCF)**: multiple cores in single cladding; parallel WDM channels.
- **Few-mode fiber (FMF)**: 2-20 modes used in parallel; mode-division multiplexing.
- **Hollow-core fiber**: light in air (lower nonlinearity + dispersion); commercial in latency-critical (HFT, satellite-uplink) since ~2020.
- **Anti-resonant + photonic-bandgap** designs.

question.question: Compute bandwidth × distance product for a fiber link
question.goal: Standard SMF at 1550 nm has chromatic dispersion D = 17 ps/(nm·km). A 10 Gbps NRZ signal has spectral width ~10 GHz = 0.08 nm at 1550 nm. Find max distance before pulse spreading equals bit period (100 ps).

steps.prompt: Pulse spread per km at given spectral width?
Maximum distance such that spread ≤ 100 ps (bit period for 10 Gbps)?
steps.reveal: Max distance ≈ 100 ps / 1.36 ps/km ≈ 73.5 km. Beyond this, intersymbol interference (ISI) degrades signal.

steps.prompt: How would you extend the reach to 1000 km at 10 Gbps?
steps.reveal: **Dispersion-compensating fiber (DCF)**: insert ~12 km of DCF with D = -100 ps/(nm·km) to cancel the +17 × 1000 = 17000 ps/(nm) accumulated. Or use **electronic dispersion compensation** in coherent receiver (modern 100G+ has 100k+ taps of digital FFE/DFE). Both common.

steps.prompt: Why is the same bandwidth-distance limit much worse at 40 Gbps?
hints: 40 Gbps spectral width is 4× wider, bit period 4× shorter.
steps.reveal: At 40 Gbps: spectral width 4× wider (0.32 nm); pulse-spread per km is 4× (5.44 ps/km); bit period is 4× shorter (25 ps). Max distance = 25/5.44 ≈ 4.6 km — 16× worse than 10 Gbps. Hence aggressive dispersion compensation required at 40G+; coherent + DSP becomes standard at 100G+.

question.question: Order these fiber-optic wavelength bands by *propagation loss* in standard silica fiber (lowest to highest).
question.explanation:
Silica-fiber attenuation:
• **1550 nm (C-band)**: ~0.2 dB/km — lowest. Telecom workhorse; EDFA-compatible.
• **1310 nm (O-band)**: ~0.4 dB/km. Zero-dispersion in standard SMF; metro + data-center.
• **850 nm (VCSEL window)**: ~3 dB/km. Multimode fiber + GaAs VCSELs; short reach.
• **1380 nm (water peak)**: ~1-5 dB/km in legacy fiber; mostly eliminated in modern fiber (low-water-peak SMF, OFS AllWave, Corning SMF-28e).
• **Visible (~600 nm)**: ~10 dB/km — Rayleigh scattering dominates; impractical for telecom.

Fundamental limit at long wavelengths: Si-O infrared absorption beyond ~2 µm. Long-term fluoride + chalcogenide fiber research pushes to ~3 µm. Hollow-core fiber bypasses limits via air-guided light.

question.question: Drag to the standard SMF attenuation (in dB/km) at 1550 nm.
question.explanation: Standard SMF at 1550 nm: ~0.18-0.22 dB/km — the lowest-loss wavelength in silica. Translates to ~10× signal reduction per 50 km without amplification. Modern ULL (ultra-low-loss) fiber (Corning Vascade, SMF-28 ULL): ~0.16-0.17 dB/km. Hollow-core fiber: ~0.5-1 dB/km but lower nonlinearity + dispersion. The 1550 nm window opened ~$1T-of-fiber-deployed industry over 30+ years.

question.question: Why is coherent detection (vs direct detection) the standard for modern 100G+ optical communication?
options: Coherent detection (I + Q + dual-polarization + local oscillator) captures full optical field (amplitude + phase + 2 polarizations), enabling: (1) higher-order modulation (16/64/256 QAM) → more bits/symbol; (2) digital signal processing for chromatic dispersion + PMD compensation in DSP rather than expensive optical equipment; (3) better sensitivity (near shot-noise limit). Combined with photonic ICs (CMOS-integrated coherent transceivers), enables 100G/400G/800G/1.6T in compact pluggable form factor.
question.explanation:
**Coherent detection revolution** (2010-onwards in telecom):

*Direct detection (legacy)*:
- Photodiode produces current ∝ |E|² (intensity only); phase lost.
- Modulation: NRZ, RZ, PAM (intensity).
- Limited spectral efficiency (~1-2 bits/symbol).
- 10G + early 40G ULH.

*Coherent detection*:
- Local oscillator (LO) laser at TX-side wavelength.
- 90° optical hybrid + balanced photodetectors → I + Q components of signal.
- Polarization-diversity (PDM/DP) → 2× channels.
- ADCs sample I + Q in both polarizations at ~100 GS/s.
- DSP equalizes + decodes everything.

*Why coherent enabled 100G+*:

1. **Higher-order modulation**: DP-QPSK (4 bits/symbol) → DP-16QAM (8 bits) → DP-64QAM (12) → DP-256QAM (16). Same baud rate, more bits.

2. **DSP-based equalization**: chromatic dispersion compensation electronically (huge filters in software; cost in DSP gates not in optics + DCF spools).

3. **PMD compensation**: dynamic; classical compensator was bulky + expensive.

4. **Near-shot-noise sensitivity**: LO heterodyning provides photon-shot-noise-limited reception. ~3 dB better than direct detection.

5. **Forward error correction (FEC)**: hard + soft decisions enable strong codes (LDPC) → near-Shannon limit on noisy channels.

6. **Carrier phase recovery**: laser linewidth tolerance via DSP.

*Industry milestones*:
- 2010: 100G DP-QPSK coherent first commercial (Nortel/Ciena).
- 2014: 200G DP-16QAM.
- 2017: 400G DP-16QAM in OpenROADM specs.
- 2020+: 800G/1.6T coherent; high-Baud (~96 Gbaud) DSP ASICs.
- 2024: 1.6T pluggable transceivers.

*Coherent in DCI + metro*:
- ZR + ZR+ coherent pluggables (QSFP-DD/OSFP form factor): 400G + 800G; cheaper LO + cooler operation; data-center interconnect (DCI).
- ZR400 widely deployed since 2022; ZR800 + ZR1600 emerging.

*PIC (photonic integrated circuit) coherent*:
- All optics on InP or Si photonic chip: LO, modulator, hybrid, photodetectors.
- Replaces ~30 discrete components with one chip.
- Enables low-cost + compact + low-power.

*DSP ASICs*:
- Modern coherent DSP: 7nm + 5nm CMOS; ~100 TOPS; ~10 W per channel.
- Marvell, Acacia, Inphi (Marvell), Ciena, Nokia, Cisco, Broadcom all compete.

*Beyond coherent*:
- **Self-coherent (Kramers-Kronig)**: simpler optical with KK relation reconstructing phase. DCI + short-reach.
- **Hollow-core + few-mode**: physical-layer evolution.

Coherent + DSP is the workhorse of all modern Tbps + Pbps optical communication. Without it, the current 100T-class fibers + global data-center scale-out would be impossible.

hints: Why does it enable higher modulation?
slides.workedSolution: Coherent detection: full optical field (I, Q, both polarizations) via local oscillator + 90° hybrid + balanced photodetectors. Enables: high-order modulation (DP-QPSK→16/64/256-QAM = more bits/symbol); DSP-based chromatic dispersion + PMD compensation; near-shot-noise sensitivity; strong FEC. 100G first commercial 2010; 1.6T pluggable 2024. PIC-coherent + DSP ASICs in 5nm CMOS now standard. Without coherent, modern 100T-class fibers impossible.

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, explain how fiber optics enabled the modern internet.
question.rubric: Mentions: fiber's combination of: (1) very low loss (~0.2 dB/km at 1550 nm) → long spans; (2) huge bandwidth (THz of available spectrum); (3) electrical isolation; (4) low cost per bit. WDM allows 100s of wavelengths in single fiber → 10s of Tbps/fiber commercially, 150+ Tbps in lab. EDFA + Raman amplifiers (1990s) replaced expensive O-E-O regenerators → enabled multi-1000 km transcontinental + transoceanic spans. Coherent + DSP (2010s) drove spectral efficiency to near-Shannon. Submarine cables (~500 active, 100s Tbps each) carry 95% of intercontinental traffic. Cost: $30-40/km (long-haul fiber install). Cumulative installed: ~5 billion km globally. Without fiber: no streaming, no cloud, no global SaaS, no AI-training data-center networks (NVLink, ZR pluggables, 800G DCI). Concludes: fiber optics is invisible infrastructure of the digital age; ~$1T cumulative investment; doubled capacity every ~2.5 yr for decades.
